overall.headline: Excellent posture — the fundamentals are all in place.

headers.title: HTTP Security Headers
headers.summary: 1 of 6 graded security headers is missing.

findings.title: 1 cookie readable from JavaScript
findings.detail: Cookies without HttpOnly can be read by any script on the page, so an XSS flaw hands over the session directly.
findings.recommendation: Add HttpOnly to any cookie your front-end code does not need to read.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy is missing
findings.detail: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are not explicitly denied, so embedded third-party frames may request them.
findings.recommendation: Send Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=() and open up only what you use.

findings.title: CSP restricts base-uri
findings.detail: Injected <base> tags cannot redirect relative URLs to an attacker-controlled host.

findings.title: CSP sets frame-ancestors
findings.detail: Framing is controlled by CSP: frame-ancestors 'none'

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is set
findings.detail: Policy defines 15 directives.
findings.evidence: default-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; child-src github.githubassets.com github.com/assets-cdn/worker/ github.com/assets/ gist.github.com/assets-cdn/worker/; connect-src 'self' uploads.github.com www.githubstatus.com collector.github.com raw.githubusercontent.com api.github.com github-cloud.s3.amazona…

findings.title: CSP uses nonces, hashes or strict-dynamic
findings.detail: Script sources are pinned per-response rather than by host allow-list — the strongest common CSP pattern.

findings.title: HSTS requests preloading
findings.detail: The preload directive is present, so the host can ship in browser preload lists.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security is set
findings.detail: max-age is 31536000s.

findings.title: HSTS covers subdomains
findings.detail: includeSubDomains extends the HTTPS requirement to every subdomain.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy is set
findings.detail: Policy is strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.title: HTTP redirects to HTTPS
findings.detail: Plain HTTP requests are sent to the encrypted site.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set
findings.detail: MIME sniffing is disabled.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options is set
findings.detail: Framing policy is DENY.

dns.summary: SPF, DKIM, DMARC and CAA are all published for github.com.

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=quarantine
findings.detail: Failing mail goes to spam rather than being rejected. A good intermediate step.
findings.evidence: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; sp=reject; pct=100; rua=mailto:dmarc@github.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc@github.com; fo=1
findings.recommendation: Once your reports are clean, move to p=reject.

exposure.title: Exposed Files
exposure.summary: Clean: 12 well-known paths checked, nothing sensitive served.

findings.title: robots.txt advertises sensitive paths
findings.detail: Disallow entries are a public list of the paths you would rather people did not visit, which is exactly where an attacker starts looking.
findings.recommendation: Protect those paths with authentication instead of naming them in robots.txt.

findings.title: Crawler directives is present
findings.detail: /robots.txt returned 200. This is expected and not a problem in itself.

findings.title: No sensitive files exposed at the well-known paths
findings.detail: Checked 12 conventional locations; none returned readable content.

findings.title: Vulnerability disclosure contact (RFC 9116) is published
findings.detail: Researchers have a documented way to report a vulnerability to you.

results.description: Environment file — typically holds database credentials and API keys
Git repository config — exposes the remote URL and often the whole source tree
Git HEAD pointer — confirms a downloadable repository
WordPress config backup — served as text, so the database password is readable
Apache configuration — reveals rewrite rules and protected paths
Subversion metadata — exposes the source tree
macOS folder index — leaks the names of files in the directory
phpinfo() output — full PHP configuration, paths and loaded modules
Apache mod_status — live request log including URLs and client IPs

findings.title: No known-vulnerable versions detected
findings.detail: Identified 1 component; none matched the scanner's advisory table.

notes: Only the first 512 KB of the page was analysed.
All checks are passive: the scanner reads public responses only. It never attempts to exploit, authenticate, brute force, or scan ports.
